h: dB = 10 log10(P2/P1) for powers (20 log10 is for voltages).
f: Step 1: ratio = 75.29. Step 2: 10 log10(75.29) = 18.77 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 32-ary modulation runs at 2715 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(32) = 5. Step 2: bit rate = 2715 x 5 = 13575 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.

q: For A = [[0, 1], [-866, -53]] (companion form), det(A) is:
h: det [[p, q],[r, s]] = p s - q r.
f: Step 1: det = (0)(-53) - (1)(-866). Step 2: = 866. Check: det(A) equals the product of eigenvalues, here the constant term of s^2 + 53 s + 866.

q: For x(t) = 927 cos(2 pi 166 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 927. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 859329/2 = 429664.5. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 166 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 194) delta(t - (-160)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(-160) = -160^2 + 194 = 25794. Check: everything away from t = -160 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 457] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 15027)
o: Memoryless and causal
With memory and noncausal
With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
Memoryless and noncausal
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 457] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {677, 448} with h[n] = {573, 296} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 382)(s + 503)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-382 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+382) + B/(s+503) with A = 1/(503 - 382) = 0.0083. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0083 e^(-382 t) - 0.0083 e^(-503 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).

q: x[n] = (0.1515)^n u[n]. The sample x[3] is:
h: Cube the base; u[3] = 1.
f: Step 1: x[3] = (0.1515)^3. Step 2: = 0.0035. Check: |a| = 0.1515 is below 1, so the ROC |z| above 0.1515 includes the unit circle: decaying and stable.

q: An odd square wave of amplitude 332 has sine harmonics (4A/(k pi)) sin(k w0 t) for odd k. The amplitude of the k = 3 harmonic is: (spaced-repetition variant 15027)
h: Substitute k into 4A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: amplitude = 4 x 332 / (3 pi). Step 2: = 140.9052 (4 decimal places). Check: it falls as 1/k, so higher harmonics weaken - the origin of Gibbs ripple concentration near jumps.

q: A 1875 Hz tone is sampled at fs = 2257 Hz. It aliases to:
h: Fold: alias = |f - k fs| for the integer k giving a result in [0, fs/2].
f: Step 1: Nyquist needs fs at least 3750 Hz, so 2257 Hz undersamples. Step 2: alias = |1875 - 1 x 2257| = 382 Hz. Check: 382 lies in [0, 1128], the representable baseband.

q: Bandwidth B = 703 kHz and SNR = 52 dB. The Shannon capacity is approximately (bps): (spaced-repetition variant 15027)
h: C = B log2(1 + SNR), with SNR converted from dB first.
f: Step 1: SNR linear = 10^(52/10) = 158489.319. Step 2: C = 703000 x log2(1 + 158489.319) which is about 12143647 bps. Check: Shannon is an upper bound; a practical rate must stay below it, then Nyquist sets the levels.

q: AM with modulating bandwidth BWm = 447.7 kHz has total transmission bandwidth: (spaced-repetition variant 15027)
h: AM keeps both sidebands: BWt = 2 x BWm.
f: Step 1: sidebands sit at fc +/- up to 447.7 kHz. Step 2: BWt = 2 x 447.7 = 895.4 kHz. Check: SSB would need only 447.7 kHz, at the cost of sharper filtering.

q: A state matrix A has characteristic polynomial lambda^2 + (-133) lambda + (4042). Its eigenvalues (the system poles) are: (spaced-repetition variant 15027)
o: 86 and 47
86 and 86
h: Factor the quadratic: (lambda - r1)(lambda - r2).
f: Step 1: lambda^2 + (-133) lambda + (4042) = (lambda - (86))(lambda - (47)). Step 2: eigenvalues are 86 and 47. Check: sum of roots = 133, product = 4042, matching trace and determinant relations.

q: Total energy of x(t) = e^(-958 t) u(t) (1 ohm reference) is: (spaced-repetition variant 15028)
h: E = integral of e^(-2a t) from 0 to infinity.
f: Step 1: square the signal: |x|^2 = e^(-1916 t) for t at least 0. Step 2: E = 1/(2a) with a = 958, so E = 0.0005. Check: finite positive energy, so this is an energy signal with P = 0.

q: For y(t) = x(38 t - 8512), the time shift (after factoring) is:
h: Rewrite as x(a (t - b/a)) and read off the shift.
f: Step 1: 38 t - 8512 = 38 (t - 224). Step 2: compression by 38 with shift right by 224. Check: the common wrong answer is 8512, the unfactored constant.

q: The system y(t) = 131 x(t) + 488 is:
o: Time-varying but linear
Nonlinear: zero input gives output 488, violating the zero-in zero-out rule
Linear: it is a straight-line graph
Memoryless, therefore linear
h: Test x = 0 first; a linear system must answer 0.
f: Step 1: with x(t) = 0 the output is 488, not 0. Step 2: superposition fails, so the system is nonlinear (affine). Check: the term 131 x(t) alone would be linear; the offset 488 breaks it.
